# Prior Lean formalizations of RH and zero-free half-planes

Follow-up to [issue #3](https://github.com/mccorvie/riemann-masullo/issues/3), checked on 20 November 2026. The earlier [arithmetic report](arithmetic.md) already identified the Axiom and Hu results for Appendix B.6. The [endgame report](endgame.md) covers the separate question of whether Masullo’s trace argument yields the claimed zero locations.

In this comparison, **Dirichlet GRH** places the critical-strip zeros of Dirichlet L-functions on `Re(s) = 1/2`. **Extended RH** makes the critical-line claim for Dedekind zeta functions of all number fields. Masullo’s [Hecke target](../../../Statements.lean) makes the critical-line claim for every unitary Hecke character of every number field, including infinite-order characters. A **quasi-RH** theorem excludes zeros in a fixed half-plane `Re(s) > θ`, where `θ < 1`. The bounds below leave part of the critical strip untreated.

The submission covers RH and Dirichlet GRH, including imprimitive characters. Alpöge describes Extended RH as a possible future extension. The Dirichlet and Hecke statements exclude the principal pole. [Scope](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/4eaee87548250b2682affda7d05d947c05554bae/lean/docs/003.md) · [Dirichlet and ζ solutions](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/4eaee87548250b2682affda7d05d947c05554bae/lean/OAI/NumberTheory/DirichletL/Nonvanishing.lean) · [Hecke solution](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/4eaee87548250b2682affda7d05d947c05554bae/lean/OAI/NumberTheory/DirichletL/Hecke/Nonvanishing.lean) | The Dirichlet theorem uses Mathlib’s `LFunction` directly and supplies a special case for B.6. The Eisenstein-field proof is a reference for the cubic-theta method. Its lattice L-function would need to be identified with our Hecke series to reuse it. |
| Dean Cureton and Jesse Thorner with AxiomProver, *A quasi-Riemann hypothesis for Dedekind zeta functions*, Thm. 1.1 and Cor. 1.2 | `DedekindZetaZeroFree.main` gives `Re(s) > 31/32` off `s = 1` for the continuation of Mathlib’s Dedekind zeta series over **every number field**. `DedekindZetaZeroFree.heckeCorollary` gives the same bound for finite-order Hecke L-functions, expressed via its own `RayClassCharacter`. It includes `s = 1` for nonprincipal characters. [Paper](https://hexagonmath.org/2610.00200v2) · [Solution](https://github.com/AxiomMath/DedekindZetaZeroFree/blob/09afbb4ce6570c1615d58509dc197fc9f0956b7d/Solution/DedekindZetaSolution.lean) | The Dedekind endpoint already agrees with the pinned API’s series in `Re(s) > 1` at the source-statement level. The finite-order corollary requires a bridge from the ray-class coefficients to the idelic character and matching Euler factors. |
| Boyang Hu, *A seven-eighths zero-free half-plane for unitary Weil L-functions*, Thm. 1.2 | `HeckeSevenEighths.heckeL_zeroFree` constructs a continuation of the ideal series with at most one simple pole on `Re(s) = 1` and proves `Re(s) > 7/8` is zero-free. It covers **every number field and every unitary Hecke character**, including infinite order, using Circle-valued idele-class characters. The cited Lean endpoint is the rank-one theorem. [Paper](https://hexagonmath.org/2610.00216v2) · [Solution](https://github.com/Rogerhu12/hecke-seven-eighths/blob/c77efa9237c4635ed61933fbca98722c359c984a/src/Solution/HeckeSevenEighthsSolution.lean) | This is the closest match for B.6.1.1 by character and field scope. The half-plane could supply nonvanishing for a logarithmic derivative there. Bounds on the derivative and reciprocal require separate estimates. |

## Verification and reuse

- **Alpöge.** The submission uses Lean 4.33.1. Andrew Sutherland reports a successful build, a three-axiom audit of all five endpoints, Lean kernel replay of the modules, and nanoda acceptance of the full export. His 19:45 UTC update records that the end-to-end Lean 4.36.0 Comparator run was still in progress after passing statement and axiom comparison. The successful Deicyde CI at the cited commit checks archive fidelity and the Mathlib-only challenge. [Sutherland’s logs and status](https://math.mit.edu/~drew/grh/) · [Mirror CI](https://github.com/Deicyde/riemann-hypothesis/actions/runs/44813916558)
- **OpenAI.** Apache-2.0, Lean 4.34.1. The cited solution bodies have no direct `sorry`. The separate challenge files deliberately use placeholders. The configurations allow `propext`, `Classical.choice`, and `Quot.sound`. MathVet reports successful Comparator runs for family 003 at the cited revision. [Dirichlet config](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/4eaee87548250b2682affda7d05d947c05554bae/lean/ComparatorChallenges/DirichletSevenEighths.json) · [Hecke config](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/4eaee87548250b2682affda7d05d947c05554bae/lean/ComparatorChallenges/HeckeSevenEighths.json) · [MathVet run index](https://math.vet/openai-math/)
- **Axiom and Hu.** Both are Apache-2.0 and use Lean 4.35.0-rc3. The cited solution bodies have no direct `sorry`. Axiom reports the standard three axioms and has a successful build of its library, challenge, and solution. Hu’s Comparator job passed with the three-axiom allowlist on commit `431028973ed592371c44293489c644480bc95ef5`, whose Git tree matches the cited solution revision. These developments share code. Axiom’s README credits adapted OpenAI material, and Hu’s README identifies Axiom’s formalization as its base and credits vendored OpenAI excerpts. [Axiom README](https://github.com/AxiomMath/DedekindZetaZeroFree/blob/09afbb4ce6570c1615d58509dc197fc9f0956b7d/README.md) · [Axiom build](https://github.com/AxiomMath/DedekindZetaZeroFree/actions/runs/38381604779/job/115243377043) · [Hu README](https://github.com/Rogerhu12/hecke-seven-eighths/blob/c77efa9237c4635ed61933fbca98722c359c984a/README.md) · [Hu Comparator](https://github.com/Rogerhu12/hecke-seven-eighths/actions/runs/42421770943/job/128551523125)
- **Local Lean 4.36.0 check.** Keep Mathlib’s `NumberField.dedekindZeta` and `NumberField.HeckeCharacter.LSeries`. For Hu’s endpoint, convert the norm-one character to a Circle-valued one, compare ramification and uniformizer coefficients using `NumberField.HeckeCharacter.IsUnramifiedAt.localValue_eq`, and identify the ideal sum with the series on `Re(s) > 1`. Propagate equality of meromorphic germs from that half-plane using `MeromorphicOn.meromorphicOrderAt_eq_top_of_isPreconnected` on the difference, then transfer the zero order with `meromorphicOrderAt_congr`. The latter steps also apply to the Dedekind endpoint on ℂ punctured at 1. The API names elaborated and the selected lemmas passed local axiom checks. The external projects were inspected at the linked revisions and have not been rebuilt on our pin. (checked locally by the scout)

For Chapters 2–3, the existing Tate and adelic Poisson precedents in [issue #3](https://github.com/mccorvie/riemann-masullo/issues/3) remain the closest matches to the paper’s analytic setup. For Chapter 13, the quasi-RH results leave zeros with `1/2 < Re(s) ≤ θ` possible, and the Alpöge submission concerns Dirichlet L-functions. The case of arbitrary unitary Hecke characters at the critical line still needs the deduction identified in the [endgame report](endgame.md).
